viz.programmableSceneBudgetNotice: This scene is taking too long to compute, so this is the last frame that finished in time.
viz.canvasLabel: Interactive visualization. Use the controls and sliders below it to change what it shows.
viz.orbitalLabel: Orbit diagram: eccentricity {eccentricity}, planet-to-star mass ratio {massRatio}, at time {time} seconds. Use the sliders below to change the orbit.
viz.trajectoryLabel: Trajectory diagram: launch speed {speed} metres per second at {angle} degrees. Use the sliders below to change the launch.
viz.trajectoryHandleLabel: Launch angle. Drag the handle, or use the arrow keys; hold Shift for bigger steps.
viz.challengeTarget: Target: land {range} m away, give or take {tolerance} m.
viz.challengeSuccess: On target! You landed {landing} m away.
viz.challengeMissShort: You landed {landing} m away, {gap} m short. Try again.
viz.challengeMissLong: You landed {landing} m away, {gap} m too far. Try again.
viz.blackbodyYAxis: Spectral radiance per unit wavelength (W m^-3 sr^-1)
viz.blackbodyFiniteRangeNote: The plotted wavelength range is finite. The left edge is 100 nm, not zero wavelength.
viz.blackbodyIdealNote: The curves show an ideal blackbody in thermal equilibrium.
viz.blackbodyCursorHint: Move the pointer or drag across the plot to read both laws at a wavelength. With the keyboard, focus the plot and use the left and right arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps).
viz.blackbodyAlt: At {temperature} kelvin, the Planck spectrum peaks near {peakWavelength} nanometres. The graph currently shows {mode}. The wavelength axis runs from 100 to 100,000 nanometres on a logarithmic scale. The Rayleigh–Jeans curve rises toward the short-wavelength edge, while the Planck curve falls.
viz.relativePeriodOrbitalAdvance: Orbital advance per mean solar day
viz.relativePeriodNoChange: The relative configuration does not change
viz.relativePeriodApparentNote: The apparent solar day varies during the year; this model shows the mean solar day.
viz.relativePeriodFacingStar: Marked meridian points at the star reference
viz.relativePeriodFacingSun: Marked meridian points at the Sun
viz.relativePeriodAlt: The {mode} model is at {cyclePosition}% of a synodic cycle. {primaryLabel} is {primaryValue}; {secondaryLabel} is {secondaryValue}; the calculated recurrence period is {synodicValue}.
viz.relativePeriodAltNoCycle: The {mode} model. {primaryLabel} is {primaryValue}; {secondaryLabel} is {secondaryValue}. There is no finite synodic period: the relative configuration does not change.
